what: U-Haul rents moving trucks and trailers to people moving house, sells boxes and towing equipment, and has become one of the largest self-storage operators in North America.
customers: Americans moving house themselves, and anyone needing storage space.
money: truck and trailer rental, self-storage and moving supplies
coverage sold with rentals and life insurance subsidiaries
moat: Twenty-three thousand locations, most of them independent dealers, which means a U-Haul is available almost anywhere in North America. No competitor has that density.
risks: 175 times earnings: profit has collapsed because people are not moving when mortgage rates are high
$1.1B of negative free cash flow, because the truck fleet and new storage must be funded
$8.2B of debt, and only three analysts cover the stock
opportunities: Analysts see about 62% upside, the widest gap in the rental sector
The self-storage portfolio has been expanding and earns far better margins than truck rental
The real estate under 23,000 locations is worth considerably more than it is carried at
watch: Truck transactions, which track house moves, and self-storage occupancy.
